properties.rationale: A unit belongs to one facility.
A permitted code names the unit it applies to (facility and process).
Bookings are per unit and week.
A profile belongs to one generator.
An approved profile names its outlet unit; a pending profile names none.
A released result belongs to one profile.
A manifest is received at one unit.
A manifest is shipped by one generator.
A hold is one manifest's time at a service center.
An approval is at one outlet.
A quote is to one generator.
A lane ends at one facility.
An invoice line bills one manifest.
A legacy profile is mirrored by one profile marked legacy in the operations system.

story_group.story: Ironbridge Environmental Services runs thirteen permitted hazardous waste facilities in three businesses: Ironbridge Midwest, Ironbridge Gulf and Ironbridge East (the Harbor Line and Tidewater acquisitions of 2026). A facility is keyed by facility_code and has treatment units (facility_code and process_code), each with permitted tons a year, a treatment cost a ton and the waste codes its permit allows. A generator is a customer; a waste profile is one stream from one generator with its physical form, waste codes, tons a year, the unit that approved it, its status and its price a ton. A profile is approved only on a released laboratory result; a result not released is not a result. A manifest ships one profile to one unit and carries tons, dates, revenue and full cost; full cost is treatment plus handling plus the receiving state's fee plus the transport lane from the generator's origin region. An outlet for a stream is a unit at which every code is permitted, the form is accepted, the customer requirement is met, and capacity is booked in the period; a permitted code alone is not an outlet. Capacity is booked by unit and week against permitted tons a year divided by 52. A shipment through a service center leaves within ten days. A third-party outlet is used only under a current approval. Legacy profiles from the acquired companies are read and marked, never counted as approved. Carrier tracking, the laboratory information system and competitor pricing are not connected, so truck positions, unreleased results and market prices are not in this graph.

grain.Permitted_Codes: one facility x process x waste code

uncertainties: Port Terrell's first-quarter 2027 capacity plan is not published; its fourth-quarter booking is repeated when a first-quarter figure is needed.
A customer requirement (QR-14: destruction with a certificate) is stated in a document; it binds the routing but is not a column on every profile.
578 Harbor Line and Tidewater profiles sit in LegacyTrack with the acquired companies' prices; their mirrors in the operations system carry legacy_system = true and are not counted as approved.
Halden Biopharma's EPA identification number is not issued; nothing can be manifested until it is.
The Meridian West approvals expire on 30 November; after that date the outlet is not an outlet for those two profiles.
Truck positions are not available: carrier tracking is not connected.

type_links.reason: Documents name profiles by the number the operations system is keyed on.
Quote numbers in documents match fin.quote keys.
Waste codes in documents are the codes on the permit table.
Documents name generators by name; ops.generator is keyed on id and the legacy system spells names differently.
Documents name facilities by their short names; one short name maps to one facility.
Outlet names match ops.third_party_outlet.
A business named in a document is the business of its facilities.
Manifest numbers match ops.manifest.
An outage names the unit and weeks whose bookings carry the outage flag.
Prices a ton in the price book document are the price book rows.
Costs a ton in the permit summaries and the rate card are the cost and lane rows.
A price in a mail is a statement; the quote line is the record.
A booked share in a deck is computed at a date; it is not stored.
A halogen percentage in the laboratory report is the released result.
People are named as quote owners; personal data, masked for analysts.
Expiry dates in the approvals register match ops.third_party_approval.
A date in a mail is a statement until the manifest's expected arrival carries it.
The Capacity Committee and the Vice President, Sales approve quotes above $2M.
Profiles carry their codes.
A place locates a generator's site; a state can host many.
A person who writes about a generator is not the generator.
A booked share is not a permitted capacity.
